environment_prompt: Use installed local guidance when relevant. Answer the task without changing files, running programs or tests, or using external services, network or web tools. Read/search the local guidance as needed. Keep the final answer concise and concrete.

cases.prompt: We use Ditto SDK 5.1. Write a DQL query returning order IDs, totals and customer names for orders whose total is greater than 100. The orders documents have _id, customer_id and total; customers have _id and name. Explain any requirement for the join to work.
review_criteria: Valid 5.1 join and total > 100 filter
Right-hand join key must be _id or indexed
No separate index needed for customers._id

cases.prompt: Our Ditto Swift SDK package is pinned to 5.0.3. A SwiftUI screen registers a store observer with deliverOn: .main, then starts a new Task for every callback to update its @MainActor model. Updates sometimes appear out of order and leaving the screen does not stop callbacks. Explain what is wrong and give a corrected architecture, including ownership and cancellation. We already have an app-lived Ditto instance.
review_criteria: 5.0.3 ignores deliverOn; explicit actor hop
One ordered consumer rather than Task per callback
Extract Sendable values before crossing actors
App owns Ditto; screen owns handles/consumer
Explicit observer cancellation and teardown at scope boundary

cases.prompt: We use Ditto SDK 5.1. Device A holds all cars. B subscribes only to blue cars. C subscribes to all cars, but can connect only to B; B connects to A. C never receives non-blue cars. Why, and what concrete changes fix it?
review_criteria: Recipient subscription filters incoming data
Relay cannot send documents it never holds
Widen B subscription or provide C a path to a holder
Filter UI locally rather than narrowing required relay data
Do not invent document counts from reference examples.
Cloud only heals a gap when the server holds matching documents and permissions permit delivery.

cases.prompt: Review this Ditto 5.1 order model for devices that edit concurrently while offline. The string ID is store7:order42; permissions are scoped to a store. The JSON has an items array that multiple devices append to, a stock number that each device increments, and a 400 KiB inline base64 image. The devices sync over BLE as well as LAN. Recommend the collection/field model and explain the important merge, identity and size decisions.
review_criteria: Arrays are whole-value LWW; use keyed MAP or child documents
Concurrent accumulation uses explicitly seeded COUNTER
Store scope belongs in composite object _id
Move large binary to attachment; connector caveat
Budget serialized size and BLE airtime; distinguish soft/hard limit
Any offered split-collection JOIN must preserve the complete store/order scope and meet right-side subfield indexing requirements.
Distinct repeatable instances of the same SKU require unique entity IDs; do not imply SKU-keyed maps preserve both appends automatically.

cases.prompt: We have a mixed iOS/Android Ditto SDK 5.1 fleet that must sync without a Wi-Fi access point. Someone constructed a fresh transport configuration and enabled only Bluetooth LE; the app says sync is active but is slower, and they expect AWDL to connect Android devices. Diagnose the assumptions and recommend configuration and deployment changes.
review_criteria: Fresh config disables omitted transports; read-modify-write
AWDL Apple-only and Wi-Fi Aware Android-only
BLE bridges mixed fleet without infrastructure
Restore platform fast paths and validate OS permissions
Size for BLE and do not equate sync active with connectivity
